land.text: Poland and Lithuania under one ruler, Cliopatria's Jagiellonian row from 1450

successors.note: A boundary of Cliopatria's rows, not an end of the kingdom: the Kingdom of Poland page runs the state to 1795, with the Union of Horodło (1413) making a joint state and the king crowned 4 March 1386 as Władysław II Jagiełło.

capitals.name: Gniezno
capitals.note: Kingdom page infobox: 'Gniezno (until 1038)'; Duchy page: 'capital in Gniezno'. Przemysł II was crowned there again on 26 June 1295.

capitals.name: Kraków
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Kraków (until 1793)'; Casimir I 'moved the capital to Kraków' (undated). Kraków was also the seat of the senior duke through the fragmentation and of Władysław I from 1306; his coronation in 1320 was there.

keyframe_review.note: 107,588 km2: Greater Poland, Kuyavia and Masovia around Gniezno. Duchy page: Mieszko I 'c. 960-992', 'centered around Gniezno'; no area on the page. Masovia and Lubusz are in the shape but not on the page.
Same shape as 962; 968 bishopric at Poznań. Unverified beyond that.

195,632 km2: Pomerania to the Baltic and the Oder, Pomerelia and half of Lesser Poland are added. The page is silent on dates; the Dagome iudex (c. 991-992) names the Baltic coast, Kraków and the Oder. Event at confidence 1.

248,543 km2: Silesia and Lesser Poland with Kraków. Bolesław I page: ruler of Lesser Poland after 977, 'reunified Poland by 995' (992 per Wiszewski); Cliopatria starts the shape in 990, two to five years early.

correction.text: valid 1003-1004 only; from 1005 the shapes _1005 and _1007 apply

keyframe_review.note: 424,991 km2 at maximum: Bohemia, Moravia, Slovakia, Lusatia and Meissen. Valid for 1003-1004 only: Bohemia fell to Jaromír on 8 September 1004 and Lusatia and Meissen were lost in 1005 (Poznań); see _1005 and _1007.

correction.text: the Polish lands of 1005-1006 without Lusatia and Meissen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1005-1006: the 1010 shape without the German part. 'According to the peace treaty Bolesław lost Lusatia and Meissen' (Poznań 1005); the 1007 re-occupation of the Lusatian marches follows. Pomerania was already out after the 1005 pagan rising.

correction.text: the shape of 1010 used from 1007: Moravia, Slovakia and the Lusatian marches, without Bohemia and Pomerania

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1007-1009: the 1010 shape as drawn. 'Bolesław re-occupied the Lusatian marches' in 1007; Cliopatria starts the shape in 1010.

303,232 km2: Moravia, the Slovak north and the Lusatian marches, no Bohemia and no West Pomerania. Fits the page: Bohemia lost 1004, Pomerania 1005, Moravia and the north of Hungary held 'until 1018', Lusatia as imperial fief from 1013 (Merseburg).

correction.text: Moravia returned in 1018, 'stayed a part of Poland until 1018'

keyframe_review.note: 288,918 km2. Lublin and the Subcarpathian lands (97%) are the Red Strongholds re-annexed in August 1018, and the Lusatian marches stay Polish at Bautzen (30 January 1018). Moravia (98% in the shape) should go in 1018: the page says it 'stayed a part of Poland until 1018'; Cliopatria keeps it to 1027.

250,439 km2. Moravia is gone and Lublin falls to 83%: the first of the losses after 1031. Casimir page: Conrad II 'regained Lusatia' (undated); Kingdom page: 1031, the kingdom 'suffered territorial losses'. Dates unverified.

113,300 km2, the low point: Greater Poland, Kuyavia and Masovia only in part, Kraków and Pomerelia gone. Casimir page: revolt and pagan revival, 1039 sack of Gniezno and Wrocław. The page dates only 1039, not the shape's 1034.

correction.text: without the Bohemian-held Silesia round Wrocław until 1050

keyframe_review.note: 183,922 km2. Silesia is at 78% in the shape, but 'Bretislaus conquered part of Silesia, including Wrocław' in 1039 and Casimir 'seized Bohemian-controlled Silesia' only in 1050. Masovia (74%) is Miecław's until 1047.

correction.text: valid 1046-1049; from 1050 the shape as drawn, Silesia seized back

keyframe_review.note: 200,878 km2. Same correction for 1046-1049: Wrocław stays Bohemian until 1050, then the shape is right. Masovia whole from 1047 ('seized the land'); Cliopatria dates it 1046.

200,900 km2 for seventy years. Quedlinburg 1054 left Silesia in Poland for a yearly tribute. Kingdom page: Bolesław II king 1076-1079; Bolesław III ruler from 1102, who divided the realm between two sons of Władysław I Herman in 1102 inside the state. No border change on the pages.

correction.text: the directly ruled realm without the Pomeranian fief (Szczecin, Wolin, Usedom)

keyframe_review.note: 256,347 km2: Gdańsk Pomerania (conquered 1115-1119) is direct land, but Western Pomerania, Wolin, Usedom and the Mecklenburg coast were a Polish fief from 1122 ('which became a Polish fief'): the vassal tint, not direct colour.

136,204 km2 for 1305-1313. The page: Sandomierz, Sieradz-Łęczyca and Brześć Kujawski by the end of 1305, Kraków on 1 September 1306, Greater Poland only 'three years later' after 1311. Valid for 1305 only as Cliopatria draws it (Wenceslaus's Polish lands, with the Czech king in personal union to 1313 in its own relation; the page has Wenceslaus III murdered on 4 August 1306); see _1306.

correction.text: Władysław's lands of 1306-1313 without Greater Poland (Henry III of Głogów's, then his sons') and without Pomerelia (a vassal tint from the end of 1306 to 13 November 1308, then the Teutonic Order's)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1306-1313: Władysław's realm without Greater Poland, which came to him in 1314 (Henry III of Głogów page: 'conquer all Greater Poland in 1314'), and without Pomerelia: 'Pomerania became subordinate to the rule of Władysław the Short as a result of an expedition at the end of 1306' (a vassal tint, ledger) and Gdańsk fell to the Teutonic Order on 13 November 1308 (Teutonic takeover page). 'By 1311, Władysław was in power in Lesser Poland and his Kuyavian patrimony.' No separate _1309 keyframe: this one already omits Pomerelia for all of 1306-1313, so a 1309 shape would be identical. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: Pomerelia was drawn as direct land here and as a vassal tint in the ledger.)

123,116 km2: Greater Poland is in ('Three years later, Greater Poland also came under his rule'); Pomerelia is out (2%). Coronation 1320. Pomerelia has been the Teutonic Order's since 13 November 1308 and is drawn contested to 1335 (ledger).

123,836 km2, no border change in the shape. 'A Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332) occupied Władysław's last years' (Władysław page). Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land were 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332' (Kalisz page): contested 1329-1332 and lost in 1332, one year before Cliopatria's 1333 shape drops them, so this shape is valid to 1331 and _1333 is read from 1332. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: was verdict ok, years 1326-1332.) [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1326..1331 from this entry's own 'valid 1326-1331 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

115,542 km2: Kuyavia down to 45% (the Teutonic conquest of Kuyavia and Dobrzyń, 'between 1329 and 1332'). Valid from 1332, one year before Cliopatria's 1333, to 1342; the land returns on 8 July 1343 (Treaty of Kalisz, ledger; see _1343). The Casimir III page has only the Visegrád verdict of November 1335 that they 'were to be returned'. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: was verdict ok, years 1333-1343.)

correction.text: the 1333 shape unchanged, valid 1332-1342: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land in the Teutonic Order's hands
the 1344 shape in 1343 only: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land back from 8 July 1343, Galicia not yet (it is assigned in 1344)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1343 only: 'King Casimir III regained Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land' by the treaty 'signed on 8 July 1343 in Kalisz'; Cliopatria shows the land back only in its 1344 shape (123,945 km2). Eastern Galicia comes in 1344 (_1344). (Added after the eu-15-b review.)

correction.text: the 1344 shape plus Galicia, Red Ruthenia, assigned to Casimir in 1344

keyframe_review.note: 123,945 km2. Galicia was assigned to Casimir in 1344 ('Volhynia was assigned to Liubartas and Galicia to Casimir'); Cliopatria gives it to Poland only in 1352.

correction.text: without the Volhynia and Podolia that the 1352 truce left to Liubartas

keyframe_review.note: 240,672 km2: Galicia (94%), Masovia whole and Volhynia and Podolia in part. The page says the 1352 truce was 'rather favourable to the Lithuanians': 'Lubartas received not only Volhynia and Podolia, but also Belz and Chełm'. Volhynia and Podolia come out until 1366. Masovia entered as a fief in 1351 on no page opened (ledger at confidence 1).

correction.text: valid 1363-1374 without Volhynia and Podolia, which the 1352 truce left to Liubartas; western Volhynia (Volodymyr, Chełm) is a vassal tint of Casimir's allies 1366-1370 in the ledger, not Polish land

keyframe_review.note: 239,794 km2. The correction of 1352 holds to 1374. In fall 1366 'Liubartas retained only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk' and Casimir gave Chełm to Yuri and Volodymyr to Aleksander, sons of Karijotas; in 1370 Liubartas 'captured all of Volhynia, including Volodymyr' (page). That western strip is recorded as a vassal tint 1366-1370 (ledger) and left out of the shape, so no _1366 keyframe. The page is silent on Podolia after 1352, so the Podolian part stays out. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: the text had Volhynia 'contested then Polish-leaning' from 1366 with no ledger event.)

230,092 km2 (Cliopatria's union with Hungary, 1375-1384), right as drawn for 1375-1377: Galicia was ruled by the Hungarian crown from 1370 but Poland and Hungary shared Louis I, and 'In 1378, Louis attached Galicia directly to the Kingdom of Hungary' (page). From 1378 see _1378. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: was adjust, removing Galicia from the whole of 1375-1384.)

New keyframe, 1378-1384: 'In 1378, Louis attached Galicia directly to the Kingdom of Hungary', so Eastern Galicia comes out of Cliopatria's 1375 shape (230,092 km2) until 'In 1387, Jadwiga attached Galicia to Poland for good' (_1385 keeps it out to 1386, _1387 brings it back). Matches the 1378 loss in the ledger. (Added after the eu-15-b review.)
229,737 km2. Galicia stays Hungarian until 'In 1387, Jadwiga attached Galicia to Poland for good'; the shape is right from 1387 (_1387). Union of Krewo 1385; Jagiełło crowned 4 March 1386.
New keyframe, 1387-1394: the 1385 shape as drawn, with Galicia back. 'In 1387, Jadwiga attached Galicia to Poland for good.'

233,778 km2. Unverified: page budget. Masovia rises to 100% and the Podlachian share to 30%, with no page opened to explain it. The Kingdom page: 'close relations' with Lithuania from the late 14th century.
233,713 km2. Unverified: page budget. Grunwald (1410) and Thorn (1411) are not on any page opened.
230,095 km2. Unverified: page budget. Union of Horodło 1413 ('transformed into a real union'), no territory. Masovia back to 96%.

285,337 km2: Podolia (88%) is added. Lithuanian Civil War page: Poland invaded Volhynia on 25 June 1431 and the Union of Grodno (15 October 1432) gave 'territorial concessions to Poland in disputed Podolia and Volhynia'. The page does not name the Podolia Voivodeship (1434) or say what Poland held afterwards; Podolia is drawn from 1431, a year ahead of Grodno, while contested.

285,384 km2, the shape of 1431. Peace of Brześć Kujawski (31 December 1435): 'The treaty did not change the borders that had been set by the Treaty of Melno in 1422.' Casimir IV approved as hereditary hospodar in 1440. Cliopatria's 1440-1449 union with Hungary (Władysław III) is on no page opened.

region.text: Greater Poland around Gniezno with Kuyavia and Masovia, the Polans' land

ledger.note: c. 960: Mieszko I rules the Polans from Gniezno. Infobox 'c. 960-992', the polity 'centered around Gniezno' with its 'capital in Gniezno'; Mieszko is the 'ruler of the Polans' who accepted Christianity in 966 (Baptism of Poland), bishopric at Poznań 968. The page gives no boundary; Cliopatria's first shape (962) is Greater Poland, Kuyavia and Masovia.

region.text: the cells Cliopatria adds in 980: Pomeranian coast to the Oder, Pomerelia, a first part of Lesser Poland and Lubusz

ledger.note: c. 980: Pomerania, the Baltic coast and the first of Lesser Poland join (Cliopatria 980). The page is silent on the date: of Mieszko I it says only that Pomerania, Silesia, Lesser Poland and Lubusz 'are not mentioned'; the Dagome iudex (c. 991-992) is quoted as running from 'the long sea' (the Baltic), naming Kraków and the Oder as boundary points, so the coast and Kraków were in by then.

region.text: Silesia and the rest of Lesser Poland with Kraków, as Cliopatria's 990 shape adds them

ledger.note: 990: Mieszko I takes Silesia and Lesser Poland from Bohemia. Mieszko I page: the conflict with Boleslaus II 'in 990, resulted in a war with Mieszko, who was supported by Empress Theophanu'; 'As a result of the conflict Silesia was taken over by Poland' ('the annexation of Silesia possibly took place around 985'); Lesser Poland: 'Possibly, Mieszko took the region before 990'. The year is the war's, as in duchy-of-bohemia /ledger/6 and Cliopatria's 990 shape. (Reviewer eu-15-b: re-dated from 992, which the Bolesław I page gives for the division of Poland after Mieszko's death, not for a Bohemian loss.)

region.text: Lusatia and Meissen, the German part of Cliopatria's 1003 shape

ledger.note: 1002: Bolesław invades Lusatia and Meissen. 'Bolesław invaded Lusatia and Meissen', seizing Bautzen, Strehla and Meissen 'with additional territories up to White Elster river'; in July 1002 Henry II 'only confirmed Bolesław's possession of Lusatia'. Fought over to the Peace of Bautzen of January 1018.

region.text: Lusatia and Meissen up to the White Elster

ledger.note: July 1002: Henry II confirms Bolesław in Lusatia. Meissen and the land to the White Elster were taken by force.

c. 1003: Moravia comes under Bolesław. 'It is also likely that Polish forces took control of Moravia and the northern parts of the Kingdom of Hungary'; the page dates the conquest '1003 or 1015' and says the area 'stayed a part of Poland until 1018'. The page does not say who held Moravia; the Bohemian duchy is the nearest neighbour in Cliopatria.

region.text: the northern parts of the Kingdom of Hungary

ledger.note: c. 1003: the north of the Kingdom of Hungary (Slovakia) comes under Bolesław ('the northern parts of the Kingdom of Hungary'; '1003 or 1015').
March 1003: Bolesław is proclaimed duke of Bohemia in Prague. 'He entered Prague in March 1003, where the Bohemian lords proclaimed him duke.'
8 September 1004: Bohemia is lost. 'The Bohemians rose up in open rebellion and murdered the Polish garrisons in the major towns'; Henry II 'made Jaromír duke of Bohemia on 8 September'.

1005: Lusatia and Meissen are lost at the peace of Poznań. 'According to the peace treaty Bolesław lost Lusatia and Meissen and likely gave up his claim to the Bohemian throne'; Henry's army had 'advanced as far into Poland as the city of Poznań'.

region.text: Pomerania, west of the Oder mouth

ledger.note: 1005: a pagan rising takes Pomerania out of Polish hands. 'a pagan rebellion in Pomerania overturned Bolesław's rule.' The page names Pomerania only; the West Pomeranian coast is the reading (Cliopatria drops it by 1010).

1007: Bolesław re-occupies the Lusatian marches. 'Henry denounced the peace, and Bolesław re-occupied the Lusatian marches', though Henry 'stopped short of retaking Meissen'. In 1013 at Merseburg Bolesław 'paid homage to King Henry for the March of Lusatia (including the town of Bautzen) and Sorbian Meissen as fiefs'.

1018: Moravia is given up. The page says the area taken in the south 'stayed a part of Poland until 1018'; the Hungarian row of the other group notes the Morava valley handed back at Bautzen. Cliopatria keeps Moravia to 1027.

region.text: the northern parts of the Kingdom of Hungary

ledger.note: 1018: the north of Hungary (Slovakia) is given up; the same 'until 1018' sentence. Cliopatria's 1018 shape holds 7% of Slovakia.
30 January 1018: the Peace of Bautzen ends the German war. The marches were kept 'not as fiefs, but as a part of Polish territory'.

region.text: the Lusatian marches kept at Bautzen

ledger.note: 30 January 1018: Bautzen leaves the Lusatian marches Polish soil, no longer imperial fiefs: 'not as fiefs, but as a part of Polish territory'.

region.text: the Red Strongholds, as Cliopatria's 1018 shape adds them: Lublin and the Subcarpathian lands

ledger.note: August 1018: Bolesław takes Kiev and re-annexes the Red Strongholds. 'Poland re-annexed the Red Strongholds, later called Red Ruthenia, lost by Bolesław's father in 981'; Kiev 'surrendered upon seeing the main Polish force on 14 August'. The page does not locate the Strongholds; the region is what Cliopatria adds in 1018 (the Lublin and Subcarpathian lands).

1025: Bolesław I crowns himself king of Poland (generally assumed Easter, 27 March 1025; Wojciechowski argues 24 December 1024). The Kingdom of Poland page: 'Bolesław I the Brave is crowned at Gniezno Cathedral, raising Poland from a duchy to a kingdom'.

1031: Mieszko II loses the crown and the kingdom shrinks to a duchy again. 'the kingdom suffered territorial losses and was effectively reduced to a duchy'; Casimir page: Mieszko 'was forced to cede the throne to Bezprym in 1031'.

c. 1031: Conrad II regains Lusatia. 'Conrad II's forces attacked Poland and regained Lusatia.' The page gives no year; 1031 is the year of the crown's loss on the Kingdom page. Cliopatria drops the German part by 1034.

region.text: the Lublin and Subcarpathian lands added in 1018

ledger.note: c. 1031-1034: the Red Strongholds fall away again. The Casimir I page is silent on Cherven/Red Ruthenia; the Kingdom page says only 'territorial losses' after 1031. Cliopatria's 1034 shape no longer holds the Lublin and Subcarpathian lands.

region.text: the realm outside the Lusatian marches and the Red Strongholds, which went in 1031: Lesser Poland, Pomerelia, part of Silesia

ledger.note: 1034-1039: the realm contracts to its core. The page describes a mass revolt and a pagan revival lasting several years (its wording, paraphrased), Lesser Poland pillaged in 1039, and Bretislaus 'sacked Gniezno'. Cliopatria's 1034 shape (113,300 km2) has lost Kraków, Pomerelia and much of Silesia; the dates are the shape's, not the page's.
c. 1038: the capital leaves Gniezno for Kraków. Kingdom page infobox: 'Gniezno (until 1038), Kraków (until 1793)'; the Casimir page says 'the capital of Poland was moved to Kraków' without a date.

1039: Bretislaus I of Bohemia invades. 'Bretislaus conquered part of Silesia, including Wrocław' and 'sacked Gniezno'; 'invaded and ravaged the country in 1039'. The page does not bound the 'part'; a radius round Wrocław is the reading.

region.text: Lesser Poland and the Silesian lands outside Wrocław, back under the duke

ledger.note: 1040: Casimir I the Restorer retakes most of the realm. Henry III 'gave him military and financial support' in 1039; with German and Kievan support he 'managed to retake most of his domain'; his reign begins in 1040 (infobox). Greater Poland and Masovia are not named as recovered.

1047: Casimir subdues Masovia. 'In 1047, Casimir started a war against Masovia and seized the land.' The rebel is named Miecław. The page adds that it is 'probable' he 're-attached Gdańsk to Poland' afterwards, undated; Cliopatria shows no Pomerelia until 1126, so it is not drawn.

1050: Casimir seizes Silesia back from Bohemia. 'Three years later, against the will of the Emperor, Casimir seized Bohemian-controlled Silesia.' At Quedlinburg in 1054 the Emperor ruled Silesia would stay in Poland for 'a yearly tribute of 117 kg of silver and 7 kg of gold'.
1076: Bolesław II regains the crown and Poland is a kingdom again; page: '1076-1079: Bolesław II regains the crown, then is excommunicated and banished'.
1079: Bolesław II is excommunicated and banished; Poland is a duchy again (Kingdom page, 1076-1079).

1115: Bolesław III invades Gdańsk Pomerania. 'The conquest of this part of the Pomeranian lands from 1115 to 1119.' Counterpart nobody: the page says 'The local rulers of the conquered Gdańsk and Słupsk were replaced by Polish nobles' and names no state there (Wartislaw I and Świętopełk I appear only at Niekładź, 1121 or 1119), and the pomerania dossier does not begin until 1138. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: counterpart was pomerania.)

1119: the conquest of Gdańsk Pomerania is complete ('from 1115 to 1119'). Counterpart nobody: the page says 'The local rulers of the conquered Gdańsk and Słupsk were replaced by Polish nobles' and names no state there (Wartislaw I and Świętopełk I appear only at Niekładź, 1121 or 1119), and the pomerania dossier does not begin until 1138. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: counterpart was pomerania.)

region.text: this part of the Pomeranian lands

ledger.note: 1119: Gdańsk Pomerania passes to Poland. Counterpart nobody: the page says 'The local rulers of the conquered Gdańsk and Słupsk were replaced by Polish nobles' and names no state there (Wartislaw I and Świętopełk I appear only at Niekładź, 1121 or 1119), and the pomerania dossier does not begin until 1138. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: counterpart was pomerania.)

1121: Bolesław marches on Szczecin. 'Bolesław's further expansion was directed to Szczecin (1121-1122).' Counterpart pomerania is Wartislaw I's Western Pomerania (page: he 'was forced to pay homage, as well as an annual tribute of 500 marks of fine silver'); the pomerania dossier starts only in 1138, so until its start moves back to c. 1121 the tint rests on this event's own region. Routed to the pomerania owner in the 2026-11-01 repair report.

1122: Western Pomerania submits. 'In 1122, Bolesław finally conquered Western Pomerania, which became a Polish fief.' Counterpart pomerania is Wartislaw I's Western Pomerania (page: he 'was forced to pay homage, as well as an annual tribute of 500 marks of fine silver'); the pomerania dossier starts only in 1138, so until its start moves back to c. 1121 the tint rests on this event's own region. Routed to the pomerania owner in the 2026-11-01 repair report.

region.text: Western Pomerania, the Oder mouth and the islands

ledger.note: 1122: Western Pomerania becomes a Polish fief ('which became a Polish fief'); Wolin and Usedom are taken in 1128-1129 and Rügen is raided in 1130 with Danish support. Counterpart pomerania is Wartislaw I's Western Pomerania (page: he 'was forced to pay homage, as well as an annual tribute of 500 marks of fine silver'); the pomerania dossier starts only in 1138, so until its start moves back to c. 1121 the tint rests on this event's own region. Routed to the pomerania owner in the 2026-11-01 repair report.

1138: the Pomeranian fief is listed as its own division. 'the country was divided between his sons into the duchies of Greater Poland, Lesser Poland, Masovia, Silesia, Sandomierz, and a Pomeranian vassal.'

region.text: Greater Poland as the Cliopatria duchy

ledger.note: 28 October 1138: Bolesław III dies and divides Poland among his sons. Died '28 October 1138'; the Testament divided the country 'among his sons, leading to almost 200 years of feudal fragmentation'. Greater Poland goes to its duchy.
1138: Masovia becomes a duchy of its own, one of the six divisions the Kingdom page names.
1138: Silesia becomes a duchy of its own, one of the six divisions the Kingdom page names.
1138: Sandomierz becomes a duchy of its own, one of the six divisions the Kingdom page names. Lesser Poland (the Kraków senior province) has no Cliopatria row and is not a separate dossier here.

26 June 1295: Przemysł II is crowned King of Poland at Gniezno, the first attempt to restore the kingdom. Przemysł II page: 'The coronation of Przemysł II and his wife Margaret took place at Gniezno Cathedral on Sunday, 26 June 1295'; he was murdered on 8 February 1296. (Reviewer eu-15-b: the Kingdom of Poland page says 'would occur in 1296'; the Przemysł II page and duchy-of-greater-poland /ledger/34 give 1295.)

1305: Władysław the Elbow-high masters Sandomierz. 'He mastered the duchies of Sandomierz, Sieradz-Łęczyca, and Brześć Kujawski by the end of the year' (settled in Sandomierz in 1304 with Hungarian help).
1305: Brześć Kujawski and Sieradz-Łęczyca come to Władysław; Wenceslaus II, 'the Czech and Polish king', died this year.

region.text: the capital of Lesser Poland, Kraków

ledger.note: 1 September 1306: Władysław enters Kraków. 'There was a festive entrance to the capital of Lesser Poland on 1 September 1306' after Wenceslaus III's murder at Olomouc on 4 August. Cliopatria's shape already holds Lesser Poland in 1305.

End of 1306: Pomerania is made subordinate. 'Pomerania became subordinate to the rule of Władysław the Short as a result of an expedition at the end of 1306.' Cliopatria draws it as direct Polish land from 1305. Drawn as a vassal tint from the end of 1306 to 13 November 1308 (the vassal_end below) and not as direct land: keyframe _1306 omits Pomerelia.

13 November 1308: Polish suzerainty over Pomerelia ends. Teutonic takeover of Danzig page: Władysław 'was only in loose control of Pomerelia and Gdańsk' (governor Bogusza); in summer 1308 a Brandenburg intervention unseated the forces loyal to Łokietek; Gdańsk 'was captured by the State of the Teutonic Order on 13 November 1308' and the Order 'seized all of Pomerelia'; the infobox has Pomerelia 'only nominally subject to Poland'. Same date as teutonic-order /ledger/6 and duchy-of-pomerelia /ledger/6; the Treaty of Soldin (September 1309) completed the Order's hold. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: was 1314 at confidence 1, Cliopatria's year, which the Władysław page does not date.)

13 November 1308: Poland and the Teutonic Order contest Pomerelia. Poland did not accept the loss: the page has lawsuits against the Order at the curia (hearings at Inowrocław and Brześć Kujawski in 1320/21 and at Warsaw in 1339) and papal rulings of 1320, 1333 and 1339 ordering Pomerelia returned, with which the Knights 'did not comply'. The dispute is drawn contested from the Order's taking of Gdańsk to the Visegrád verdict of November 1335. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: was 1314 at confidence 1.)

1314: Władysław conquers all of Greater Poland. 'Władysław I the Elbow-high was able to conquer all Greater Poland in 1314' (Henry III of Głogów page); the Władysław page has only 'Three years later, Greater Poland also came under his rule' after 'By 1311'. Henry III held Poznań and Gniezno 1305-1309 and Kalisz 1307-1309 (infobox), and the infobox lists his sons (Henry IV the Faithful, Konrad I, Bolesław, Jan, Przemko II) as successors; the page says they 'soon split between them the inheritance', the fragmentation 'visible especially in the Greater Poland region'. Counterpart duchy-of-g-ogow, the duchy of Henry III and his heirs; the page does not say which son held which part in 1309-1314. Mirror: duchy-of-g-ogow /ledger/9 closes Henry III's tenure in 1309 and records no 1314 loss. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: counterpart was duchy-of-greater-poland, which ended in 1304; source was the Władysław page, c2.)

January 1320: Władysław I is crowned in Kraków and the kingdom is restored. 'fully restored under Władysław I the Elbow-High'; the Elbow-high page gives 20 January 1320 in the infobox and 30 January in the text.

1329: the Teutonic Order begins the conquest of Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land. Treaty of Kalisz (1343) page: the land was 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332' (no months given); Płowce, 27 September 1331, was fought in Kuyavia (Władysław I page). Matches teutonic-order /ledger/9. (Revised after the eu-15-b review: was a 1333 contest_start at confidence 1, read from Cliopatria's 1333 shape.)
1332: the conquest is complete and the land is held, not fought over, until the 1343 peace ('between 1329 and 1332'). Matches teutonic-order /ledger/11.

1332: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land pass to the Teutonic Order, 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332' (the page gives the range, not the month). Cliopatria's shape drops them one year later, in 1333. Matches teutonic-order /ledger/10 (gain from kingdom-of-poland, 1332) and /ledger/13 for the 1343 return.

November 1335: the Visegrád arbitration. Casimir was 'forced to renounce Pomerania and the Chełmno Land', declared 'a perpetual alms of the King of Poland to the Teutonic Order'; Trenčín, 24 August 1335, had the Luxembourgs ready to renounce the title of Kings of Poland. The Teutonic takeover page adds that a war ensued in the late 1330s and that Casimir undertook to raise no future claims on Pomerelia only in the Treaty of Kalisz, 8 July 1343 (Kalisz page): the Casimir page's Visegrád date is kept for the end of the contest. No 1335 loss is recorded: the land left Polish control on 13 November 1308 (the vassal_end and contest_start above) and is not in the shape after 1308. teutonic-order has no 1335 event for it, only its 1308 gain from kingdom-of-poland (/ledger/6).

June 1340: Casimir III takes Lviv. After the murder of Yuri Boleslav Casimir first invaded within days; in June he 'conquered Lviv and burned down the Lviv High Castle' and agreed terms with Dmytro Dedko's nobles. The Casimir III page says he 'later became King of Ruthenia in 1340'.

8 July 1343: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land return to Poland by the Treaty of Kalisz ('King Casimir III regained Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land'); Casimir 'undertook to raise no future claims on Pomerelia, as well as Chełmno Land and Michałów Land'. Cliopatria shows them back in 1344. (Reviewer eu-15-b: re-dated from 1344.) The land was lost to the Order in 1332 (the loss above); the 1344 return in Cliopatria's shape is one year late.
1344: Poland and Lithuania make peace over Galicia-Volhynia: 'Volhynia was assigned to Liubartas and Galicia to Casimir'.

1344: Galicia (Red Ruthenia) goes to Casimir III ('Galicia to Casimir'). Cliopatria's Polish shape takes it only in 1352, when its Galicia-Volhynia row has ended; the Casimir III page's infobox dates the Ruthenian reign '1349-1370'.

1348: Volhynia becomes the object of the Polish-Hungarian-Lithuanian war. After the Teutonic Knights beat Lithuania at Strėva, Liubartas lost territory to Casimir and Louis I except eastern Volhynia with Lutsk (page, paraphrased). The 1352 truce gave Liubartas Volhynia, Podolia, Belz and Chełm back.

1352: Masovia enters the Polish shape. Neither the Kingdom page nor the Casimir III page mentions Masovia (the Casimir page lacks the 1351 Masovian homage); Cliopatria's Masovia row ends in 1351 and its Polish shape takes Masovia whole in 1352. The Galicia-Volhynia page has Casimir allied with Siemowit III of Masovia in 1366, which reads as an ally or vassal rather than annexed land.

Autumn 1366: Casimir III beats Liubartas. Casimir, 'allied with Siemowit III of Masovia', resumed the war and Liubartas 'retained only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk' and became somewhat dependent on Poland.

ledger.counterpart: Yuri and Aleksander, sons of Karijotas
ledger.note: Autumn 1366: western Volhynia passes to Casimir III's allies. 'In fall 1366, a treaty was signed: Liubartas retained only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk'; Casimir rewarded his allies: Yuri, son of Karijotas, received Chełm, and his brother Aleksander received Volodymyr (Yuri, son of Narimantas, kept Belz). The page does not call them vassals; read as Polish clients because Casimir disposed of the land and Liubartas was left 'somewhat dependent on Poland'. Drawn as a tint, not as Polish land (keyframe _1363 omits Volhynia). grand-duchy-of-lithuania records only a 1366 contest_end for this treaty, no loss. (Added after the eu-15-b review.)

ledger.counterpart: Yuri and Aleksander, sons of Karijotas
ledger.note: 1370: Liubartas retakes western Volhynia. 'In 1370, Liubartas took advantage of Casimir's death and captured all of Volhynia, including Volodymyr.' The page is silent on Chełm after 1366. (Added after the eu-15-b review.)
5 November 1370: Casimir III dies and the Piast line ends; Louis I of Hungary of the House of Anjou 'became king in 1370'.

1378: Louis attaches Galicia directly to Hungary. Galicia was ruled by the Hungarian crown 1370-1387 with Vladislaus II of Opole as regent, and in 1378 Louis attached it directly to the Kingdom of Hungary (page, paraphrased). Cliopatria keeps Galicia in the Polish shape throughout. Before 1378 Galicia was ruled by the Hungarian crown but Poland and Hungary were in personal union under Louis I (page: 'Between 1370 and 1387, Galicia was ruled by the Hungarian crown'), so it is drawn Polish through 1377.
4 March 1386: Jogaila is crowned Władysław II Jagiełło, the Jagiellon dynasty begins after the Union of Krewo (1385) and his marriage to Queen Jadwiga.
1387: Galicia returns to Poland for good. 'In 1387, Jadwiga attached Galicia to Poland for good.' The 1392 Ostrów Agreement then settled Galicia for Poland and Volhynia for Lithuania.

25 June 1431: Poland invades Volhynia. 'the Polish army invaded Volhynia' and took 'part of Volhynia, Horodło, Volodymyr-Volynskyi, and Zbarazh'. Podolia and Volhynia were to be Lithuania's 'only during the lifetime of Vytautas' (Polish reading).
15 October 1432: the Union of Grodno. Sigismund 'made territorial concessions to Poland in disputed Podolia and Volhynia'; a truce of 1 September 1431 had run to 24 June 1433.
15 October 1432: Podolia and part of Volhynia pass to Poland by the Union of Grodno. The page gives no details; Cliopatria's Polish shape has Podolia from 1431.

region.text: the Crown of Poland as Cliopatria draws it in its last years

ledger.note: 1449: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends and its House of Jagiellon row (Poland with Lithuania in one union) begins in 1450. The Kingdom itself did not end: the page runs it to 1795 with the Union of Horodło in 1413 making a joint state.

wars.name: German-Polish War of 1002-1018 (Lusatia, Meissen, Bohemia)

zones.text: Lusatia and Meissen to the White Elster

wars.outcome: Peace of Bautzen, 30 January 1018: Bolesław kept the Lusatian marches 'not as fiefs, but as a part of Polish territory'. Lusatia and Meissen were lost at Poznań in 1005 and re-taken in 1007, Bohemia was lost on 8 September 1004, a homage for Lusatia and Meissen was paid at Merseburg in 1013, and the army of Henry II won at Ciani in 1015.
wars.note: No page for the war itself was opened; the entry rests on the Bolesław I page. The war's Wikipedia title was not checked.

wars.name: Kiev expedition of 1018

zones.text: the Red Strongholds, as Cliopatria's 1018 shape adds them

wars.outcome: Bolesław captured Kiev (it 'surrendered upon seeing the main Polish force on 14 August'), installed his son-in-law Sviatopolk I, and re-annexed the Red Strongholds, 'later called Red Ruthenia'. Sviatopolk 'lost the throne soon afterwards'.
wars.note: The page does not say whether Polish control of Kiev outlasted Sviatopolk, nor where the Strongholds lay.

wars.name: Bohemian invasion of 1039 and Casimir's restoration
wars.outcome: Bretislaus I sacked Gniezno and took part of Silesia with Wrocław in 1039; Casimir I returned with German and Kievan support in 1039-1040, seized Silesia in 1050 and at Quedlinburg in 1054 the Emperor left it to Poland for a yearly tribute of 117 kg of silver and 7 kg of gold. A treaty with Bretislaus was signed at Regensburg in 1042.
wars.note: The page gives 1039 for the invasion, not 1038-1039; 1055 is not on it.

wars.name: Casimir I's war against Masovia
wars.outcome: 'In 1047, Casimir started a war against Masovia and seized the land.' The rebel is Miecław, whose Pomeranian allies Casimir defeated; Gdańsk was 'probably' re-attached to Poland, undated.

wars.name: Bolesław III's conquest of Pomerania

zones.text: Western Pomerania, a Polish fief from 1122

wars.outcome: Gdańsk Pomerania conquered 1115-1119, Szczecin 1121-1122, Western Pomerania made a Polish fief in 1122, Wolin and Usedom taken with Danish troops in 1128-1129, an expedition to Rügen in 1130; the Merseburg congress of 1135 addressed Pomerania.
wars.note: The page does not give a homage of 1135 for Pomerania; it names the congress only. Belligerent pomerania stands for Wartislaw I's Western Pomerania (1121-1122); the 1115-1119 rulers of Gdańsk Pomerania are 'nobody' in the ledger.

wars.name: Bolesław III's wars with Bohemia and Hungary
wars.outcome: Svatopluk made duke of Bohemia on 14 May 1107; Hundsfeld, 24 August 1109 (historians doubt it); 'a decisive victory against the Czechs at the Battle of Trutina on 8 October 1110'; a Bohemian-Hungarian-Rus coalition 'achieved complete victory over the Polish duke' at the Sajó on 22 July 1132. No border change is dated.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer sees they were considered. The Hungarian row of the other group has a cell change of 1139 against Poland.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: 'A Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332) occupied Władysław's last years'; Płowce, Kuyavia, 27 September 1331. Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land were 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332' and returned to Poland by the Treaty of Kalisz, 8 July 1343 (Kalisz page). The Visegrád verdict of November 1335 said they 'were to be returned', and Pomerania and the Chełmno Land were renounced.
wars.note: Conquest dates and the 1343 return from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Kalisz_(1343); they match teutonic-order /ledger/9-13. The Władysław page gives no outcome. (Revised after the eu-15-b review.)

wars.name: Galicia-Volhynia Wars
wars.outcome: Lviv taken June 1340; 1344 peace 'Volhynia was assigned to Liubartas and Galicia to Casimir'; 1348 Liubartas loses land except eastern Volhynia with Lutsk; 1352 truce 'rather favourable to the Lithuanians'; 1366 Liubartas beaten and left only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk, western Volhynia (Volodymyr, Chełm) to Casimir's allies; 1370 Liubartas retakes all Volhynia; Galicia under the Hungarian crown 1370-1387; 1387 Jadwiga attached Galicia to Poland for good; 1392 Ostrów Agreement: Galicia to Poland, Volhynia to Lithuania. 'Poland acquired a territory of approximately 52,000 square kilometres'.
wars.note: The page is silent on Podolia after 1352, on any 1349 event, and on Jadwiga's 1387 move as a reconquest.

wars.name: Polish intervention in the Lithuanian Civil War (1431-1432)
wars.outcome: Polish army invaded Volhynia on 25 June 1431 and took part of Volhynia, Horodło, Volodymyr-Volynskyi and Zbarazh; the Teutonic Knights were beaten at Dąbki on 13 September 1431; truce of 1 September 1431 'more favorable to Poland'; Union of Grodno, 15 October 1432: 'territorial concessions to Poland in disputed Podolia and Volhynia'.
wars.note: The page lists the Peace of Brześć Kujawski (31 December 1435) as leaving the Treaty of Melno borders of 1422 unchanged; it does not say what Poland held afterwards.

certainty.note: Piast frontiers on the Oder, the Baltic, the Carpathians and the Bohemian and Rus' marches are approximate. The Dagome iudex (c. 991-992) is the one document that names bounds. The marches of Lusatia and Meissen were fixed at Bautzen on 30 January 1018 but held only to 1031.
No Cliopatria shape: the land is the duchies' (their own dossiers). Only titles remain here (Przemysł II crowned 26 June 1295).
The Teutonic frontier (Visegrád 1335) and the Galician-Volhynian line (1392 Ostrów Agreement) are treaty lines the pages name but do not draw; Podolia and Volhynia stay soft.

notes:
Page budget (9 pages) fully spent. No page opened gives an infobox area for the kingdom, so areas could not be compared; Cliopatria's range is 107,588 (962) to 424,991 km2 (1003). The Casimir III page says only that he 'managed to double the size of his kingdom'; the Galicia-Volhynia page puts the Galician gain at about 52,000 km2, against Cliopatria's jump from 123,945 (1344) to 240,672 km2 (1352).

CLIOPATRIA ROW. 'Kingdom of Poland' 962-1449 has no shape for 1139-1304; those years belong to the Duchies of Poland rows (Greater Poland, Masovia, Sandomierz, Silesia, Łęczyca, Opole and others, other dossiers). The dossier keeps one state across the gap: split events on 28 October 1138 name the four duchies the Kingdom page lists and have matching found events in their dossiers; Lesser Poland (the senior province round Kraków, 1138-1279) and the Pomeranian vassal have no row of their own. The row ends 1449 where Cliopatria's 'House of Jagiellon' row begins; the state itself continued to 1569 and 1795 (Kingdom page), so the 1449 dissolve is a row boundary, confidence 1. The polish-lithuanian-commonwealth and house-of-jagiellon dossiers belong to other parts of eu-15.

WRONG OR SUSPECT SHAPES (verdict adjust): 1003 (Bohemia lost 1004, Lusatia 1005), 1018 (Moravia kept to 1027 instead of 1018), 1040 and 1046 (Wrocław Silesia Bohemian to 1050), 1126 (Western Pomerania was a fief, not direct), 1305 (Greater Poland drawn 1305-1313 though the page has it c. 1314; also Cliopatria's 1305-1313 Bohemian personal union against the page's 4 August 1306 murder of Wenceslaus III), 1344 (Galicia from 1344, Cliopatria 1352), 1352 and 1363 (Volhynia and Podolia: the 1352 truce left them to Lithuania), 1375 and 1385 (Galicia Hungarian 1378-1387).

NOT SETTLED (page silent, kept at confidence 1): the dates of the early growth (980, 992), who held Moravia in 1003, Cherven and Lusatia in 1031, the 1034 contraction, Masovia as a Polish fief in 1351-1352, the fate of Podolia 1352-1430, the shapes of 1395, 1402 and 1415 (unverified: page budget), the Hungarian union 1440-1444. Pages a gap-filler should open: History of Poland (966-1385) (the title did not load), Peace of Thorn (1411), Polish-Teutonic War (1409-1411), Union of Krewo, Duchy of Masovia, Cherven Cities, Treaty of Bautzen, Podolia Voivodeship.

RULERS: the strip is left out. The pages opened give only scattered reigns (Mieszko I c. 960-992, Bolesław I 992-1025, Bezprym 1031, Casimir I from 1040, Bolesław II 1076-1079, Bolesław III 1102/1107-1138, Przemysł II crowned 26 June 1295 (murdered 1296), Władysław I 1306/1320-1333, Casimir III 1333-5 November 1370, Louis I 1370-1382, Jadwiga 1382, Jagiełło crowned 4 March 1386); a continuous list from 'List of Polish monarchs' should be added.

DYNASTY CHANGES inside the state are rename events (Duchy and Kingdom in 1025, 1031, 1076, 1079, 1295, 1320; Piast to Anjou 1370; Anjou to Jagiellon 1386).

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: Miecław's Masovia (1040-1047, a rebel state; the page names only Miecław's war of 1047); the Kraków senior province 1138-1279.

GAZETTEER: all names used resolve. Missing as historical regions: Lusatia, Meissen, the Red Strongholds (Cherven Cities), Dobrzyń Land, Chełmno Land, Sieradz-Łęczyca; the dossier uses intersections of Cliopatria shapes with Germany, Lublin and Subcarpathian, and the region Kuyavia / Pomerelia as stand-ins.

REPAIR OF 2026-11-01 (after the eu-15-b review). Pomerelia: Polish control ends 13 November 1308 (Teutonic takeover page), drawn as a vassal tint from the end of 1306 and not in keyframe _1306; the contest with the Order runs 1308-1335 and the 1335 loss is dropped. Kuyavia and Dobrzyń: contest 1329, lost 1332, returned 8 July 1343 (Kalisz page); _1326 and _1333 are read one year earlier than Cliopatria and _1343 is new. Greater Poland 1314: counterpart duchy-of-g-ogow (Henry III's heirs). Gdańsk Pomerania 1115-1119: counterpart nobody. Galicia: _1375 is ok (1375-1377), _1378 new (1378-1384). Western Volhynia: vassal tint of Casimir's allies 1366-1370, not in the shape. Still open: the Western Pomerania vassal (1121-1138) names pomerania, whose dossier begins in 1138; the Masovian fief of 1351 is still a 1352 gain at confidence 1.
